contract.note: Repeated documented incidents during May are a fair ordinary reading of the statement. The illustrative frequency threshold does not require interpreting routine as a large share of all filings.

evidence.note: Reports at least 23 judicially flagged incidents during May. The count includes fabricated quotes and other authorities as well as cases, but supports a recurring pattern of hallucinated legal citations.
The May 27 article says last month, which refers to April. Its 13-of-23 professional attribution cannot be assigned to May as the item's metadata and explanation claim.

reviews.rationale: The reported May count and dated sanctions example support repeated incidents under the contract's ordinary reading. The April professional breakdown cannot establish May's lawyer share, and the packet does not establish prevalence among all filings. Neither limitation defeats the recurring-incidents claim.
